description.narrative:
The Influencing Just Energy Transition (I-JET) project is a five-year regional initiative (2022–2027) led by Oxfam and partners to support a gender-just, inclusive, and sustainable energy transition across Southeast Asia. With ASEAN countries among the most climate-vulnerable globally and still heavily reliant on fossil fuels, the project aims to shift regional and national energy policies toward renewable energy (RE) solutions that are equitable, community-owned, and environmentally responsible.
I-JET focuses on empowering CSOs, particularly women-led groups, People with Disability, and socially marginalised communities, to actively engage in shaping energy transition narratives and policies. The project promotes the integration of gender equality, social inclusion, and human rights due diligence into energy frameworks, ensuring that the benefits of the transition are shared fairly and that no one is left behind.
Working in partnership with the ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE), Climate Action NetworkSoutheast Asia (CANSEA), and national CSOs in Cambodia, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Indonesia, I-JET supports advocacy for ambitious renewable energy targets, increased investment in community-owned RE projects, and the adoption of just transition principles in ASEAN’s energy roadmap (third phase of the ASEAN Plan for Energy Cooperation – APAEC 2026-2030).
The project is a with Oxfam’s strategic priorities through applying a justice lens across climate, gender, economic and energy dimensions. It also aligns with global climate goals and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those related to gender equality, clean energy access, and climate action.
Through regional and national convenings, policy engagement, and strategicpartnerships, I-JET seeks to influence ASEAN’s energy future—ensuring itis not only low-carbon but also inclusive, participatory, and transformative for all communities.

participating-org.narrative:
ACE was established in 1999 as an inter-government body through an ASEAN agreement with a mandate to “[1] unify and strengthen ASEAN Energy Cooperation by providing a platform for sharing, policy advisory, best practices, and capacity building; [2] provide a knowledge repository for ASEAN Member States (AMS) and services through data management, publication and dissemination; and [3] assist AMS on research and identifying practical <(>&<)> specific solution on policies, legal <(>&<)> regulatory frameworks, technologies, and innovative solutions”.
It envisions to be “a catalyst for the economic growth and integration of the ASEAN region by initiating and facilitating multilateral collaborations and joint and collective activities on energy” with a mission of accelerating “the integration of energy strategies within ASEAN by providing relevant information and expertise to ensure the necessary energy policies and programmes are in harmony with the region’s economic growth and environmental sustainability”.
Oxfam is ACE’s first CSO partner and will refer to its partnership arrangement with Oxfam as its template in exploring similar arrangements with other CSOs.
A partnership arrangement with the ASEAN Center of Energy (ACE) was initiated in the last quarter of the I-JET project’s Year 2 (2023-2024) to support Oxfam’s initiative of enabling a just energy transition in the ASEAN, After a series of exploratory meetings between ACE and the I-JET PMU, it was agreed by both parties that they share a common aspiration of promoting just energy transition in the ASEAN and agreed to enter into a partnership. The partnership was formalized through the signing of a Memorandum of Agreement between Oxfam and ACE on 07 May 2024, by Oxfam International-Asia Regional DirectorJohn Samuel in behalf of Oxfam and by Executive Director Dr. Nuki Agya Utama in behalf of ACE.
The MOU is effective from 07 May 2024 until 30 June 2027 and will cover Year 3-5 of the I-JET project (01 July 2024-30 June 2027).
Following Oxfam’s internal protocols, the partnership will be managed by a Partnership Management team that is composed of designated representatives from Oxfam in Indonesia as the lead and the I-JET who will support Oxfam in Indonesia in managing the partnership.
Subsequently, a Partnership Capacity Assessment was conducted by Oxfam in Indonesia as prescribed by OGB regulations where ACE was found to be compliant with the project and donor requirements. ACE started working with the I-JET project and other project partners in Year 3 (01 July 2024-30 June 2025) and has submitted a project proposal for this purpose that was subsequently accepted and approved by the PMU that resulted in the following key outcomes:
1- The convening of the first Strategic Multi-stakeholder Forum on Just and Inclusive Energy Transition in ASEAN as a side event to the 24th ASEAN Energy Business Forum 2- The publication of the 8th ASEAN Energy Outlook report with inputs from Oxfam and partners 3- The publication of the Guide to a Just and Inclusive Energy Transition in the ASEAN
At the conclusion of Year 3 and in consideration of the ongoing transition of Oxfam in Indonesia towards affiliation through the Penabulu Foundation, it was agreed that the I-JET PMU will directly manage the partnership with ACE in close coordination with the Penabulu Foundation for Year 4 onwards.
This required the transitioning of ACE from the OGB system into the ONL system, and the initiation of a PRISMA process where ACE is found to be fully compliant to Oxfam and donor requirements with low risk areas that can be mitigated.
Parallel to this is ACE’s submission and the I-JET PMU’s acceptanceand approval of its proposed plan and budget for Year 4 since ACE is already a partner albeit being migrated from the OGB system tothe ONL system.
